# Trace idle reduction — BLOCK

Subject `plan:nav-trace-idle`; request `01a1ce96-a292-7c03-bfc9-2dbff8486d09`.  
Head `8c451497f4fa452249ebcb8cb32ac91c053f572d`; parent `d98cb715ae8611c127d3b380a66e077c1e8b7f39`.  
Retained author build `pMh2FQWf7fwyDSsj1GFcN`, worktree `/Users/jordanknight/substrate/chainglass-trace-idle-r`.

## Findings

|Severity|Location|Consumer-visible defect|
|---|---|---|
|P2|`use-panel-state.ts:101–107`; `changes-snapshot.ts:33–37`|Tree-mode refresh no longer updates `workingChanges`, although browser attention and desktop/mobile search badges consume it outside Changes.|
|P2|`use-panel-state.ts:58–60,77–85`|Loaded refs are never reset for a changed worktree; the same browser retains old-worktree changes and does not request the new snapshot.|
|P2|`use-panel-state.ts:121–136`|Visibility resume bypasses the scheduler and retains a pending timer. Automatic refreshes can run 1000 ms, or only 200 ms, apart despite the stated minimum 2000 ms.|
|LOW|`rs-event-stream.ts:132–142`|A hello-only planned recycle incorrectly marks the next first/recovery connection as `afterRecycle`, suppressing its claimed info-level log at debug. No transport/data-loss defect was established.|

### 1. Keep always-live consumers fresh outside Changes

`BrowserClient` sends `workingChanges.length` to `WorkspaceContext.setHasChanges` at 741–743 and passes the array to desktop search at 1551 and mobile search at 1771. `workingChanges` therefore is not Changes-panel-only data. Only `recentFiles` can be made panel-only without replacing the other consumers' status source.

Independent retained-build proof on owned localhost 3199: load an owned untracked file in Changes, switch to Tree, delete the owned file, then observe an actual file-event `fetchChangesSnapshot` request succeed with HTTP 200 and body `{tree:true,changes:false}`. Git state was clean, yet the tab still showed the dirty `❗`. `/tmp/reviewer-trace-stale-attention-proof.json` records that successful refresh and title. Source also shows why status badges stay stale; mobile badge loss is source-reviewed, not a separate mobile visual proof.

**Baseline correction:** the old code already had an initial-mount workingChanges gap. The newly introduced regression is skipping its update on refresh while Tree is selected—not the initial gap itself. The author confirmed this distinction. Initial/no-Changes screenshots are supporting observations, not proof that the mount gap was introduced here.

### 2. Reset snapshot identity on worktree change

The server page renders BrowserClient without a worktree key (`page.tsx:81–89`); BrowserClientInner is likewise unkeyed (`browser-client.tsx:155–176`). Its real switcher changes the worktree query through router.push (`202–212`), preserving the hook. The loading effect observes a new load callback but returns because both loaded refs still describe the previous worktree.

Independent actual switch: after loading the owned trace-worktree change, switch through the real dropdown to clean `chainglass-icons` / branch `icons-cache`. The URL and header identify icons-cache, yet Changes still renders `? reviewer-trace-status-fixture.txt`, a path absent from that target worktree. `/tmp/reviewer-trace-worktree-proof.json` and inspected `/tmp/reviewer-trace-worktree-ghost.png` preserve the phantom row. The focused real-hook probe also rerendered `/A→/B` and retained `a.ts`, with only `/A` ever requested; expected `b.ts` failed.

Reset/guard state by worktree identity, including completion of earlier in-flight loads; do not make a new path depend on a later file event or manual refresh.

### 3. Enforce one timing policy across visibility transitions

Two independently executed controlled-clock probes use the real hook:

- A visible event schedules t=2000; hide+another event at 500; show at 1000. Resume refreshes at 1000, and the original timer refreshes again at 2000: **1000 ms spacing**.
- First automatic refresh completes at 2000; hide+event at 2100; show at 2200. With no pending timer to cancel, resume refreshes at 2200: **200 ms spacing**.

Canceling a pending timer only fixes the first duplicate. The second requires a last-refresh spacing policy shared by resume and ordinary change-driven scheduling. The explicit manual button may remain immediate.

The first probe also contains the worktree test: two expected failures, 17:23:40, 2.41 s. The separate completed-refresh probe failed at 17:29:12, 1.37 s. These are deliberately failing reviewer regression probes against the submitted head, not failures hidden from its verdict. Copies are `/tmp/reviewer-trace-hook.test.tsx`, `/tmp/reviewer-trace-spacing.test.tsx`; structured results `/tmp/reviewer-trace-hook-proof.json`. All copies inside the author worktree were removed. The first diagnostic's exact-two-call observation is not a permanent regression-test requirement: a correct coalescing implementation can make only one call.

### 4. Preserve first/recovery connection logging across hello-only recycles

A hello frame does not establish a reported connection (`rs-event-stream.ts:103–105`), but either planned-recycle branch sets afterRecycle true regardless of establishment. A later first cursor then produces connected(afterRecycle=true), mapped to debug by `start-pij-poller.ts:190–194` even for the first reported connection or first recovery after a failure.

A real native-fetch HTTP/NDJSON fixture reproduced both sequences. This is a LOW operational logging defect, not another transport blocker. Preserve the initial/post-failure info obligation until a reported connection actually consumes it.

## Positive behavior and verification

**59 existing targeted tests / six files passed**: event stream 13, panel state 5; note writer 12, note reader 10, working-status parser 10, ChangesView 9. Two runs: 18 tests at 17:19:50 (1.59 s), 41 at 17:32:51 (3.58 s). No reviewer FFT, production build, lint or formatter was run.

**Notes:** seeded two owned notes through the existing real persistence API: one open, one complete. Before opening the overlay, the instrumented page made **zero `fetchNotes` requests**. First open issued two successful queries (filtered list and unfiltered totals), not two mounts. The actual panel showed **1 open · 1 complete**. Switching to Complete showed only the completed note while retaining both global totals. `/tmp/reviewer-trace-notes-proof.json` and inspected `...-notes-counts.png`. Independent tree/PR note indicators remain on their own fetch paths; direct Add Note still enables the modal through isModalOpen→hasOpened, source-reviewed. Both owned note IDs were deleted; the newly created empty data file was removed. No unrelated note data existed or was deleted.

**Deleted marker:** an owned disposable real Git repository contained a committed file which was then removed. The retained build's combined action returned HTTP 200, and the actual Changes surface rendered the red **D reviewer-deleted.txt** row and one-file deletion stat. `/tmp/reviewer-trace-deleted-marker-proof.json` and inspected `...-deleted-marker.png`. The temporary Git repository was removed. No tracked product file was deleted. This exercises initial combined-action delivery/rendering, not a live watcher attached to an unregistered temporary repository. Live event delivery was separately exercised in the registered trace worktree above; the author event probe also records the visible/hidden/deletion request sequence.

**Stream recovery:** actual `createRsClient` + native fetch + actual `createRsEventStream`, private temporary daemon.key, owned loopback HTTP/NDJSON endpoint. Apply cursor 100, destroy the socket and listener, rotate the key and rebind the same port. The client resumed `since={machine:100}` with the new bearer and applied 101 at **360.846 ms**, before the original socket's **5087.604 ms** shortened recycle deadline. A subsequent shortened real planned recycle resumed from 101 and applied 102 without another failure status. First/recovery connections mapped to info; planned connection mapped to debug. Hello-only diagnostics then reproduced the LOW defect. Full transcript `/tmp/reviewer-trace-stream-smoke.log`; source-pinned probe SHA-256 `2100003bd39e841825357c32bfd6fee6782e70c638b9fa3cf167469cf84e7c73`, run duration 8.43 s. Exit zero means transport passed AND both logging defects reproduced, not a clean-product result.

The production default is source-verified **600000 ms**; shortened timers were used in the fixture. The wire is NDJSON with a JSON `since` query, not SSE/Last-Event-ID. All fixture sockets/listeners/keys were cleaned. **Ceiling:** no actual shared/native pij daemon was restarted, no real adapters or poller.ingest/browser propagation exercised by that fixture, and debug/info is the reviewed bootstrap mapping rather than captured bootstrap console output. A supported HTTP disconnect/key-rotation/resume contract was exercised; no ten-minute or hour-long timing claim.

## Author gates, composition and idle evidence

`TraceGateReview` read the ENTIRE `/tmp/trace-idle/fft.log` raw contiguous 1–4309 through EOF and all fft.meta: **353218 bytes**, SHA-256 `3029c5765286f542fb54b4bfb4ee747b59af68952db785b347d71656697599f2`. Meta hash `26b8033e2dccd661c1bf3a45c03c1fc45c308780ef9ccc506a4f451832fe4537` records **16:59:22–17:07:04 / exit 0 / load 43.05→25.04**. Six gates passed: 1806 lint/format files, seven build tasks with web/CLI executed and five cache replays, all nine configs, **552 files / 7307 tests passed / 60 skipped**, audit 3 low/16 moderate and no high/critical. Warnings include 28 missing icons, three Turbopack tracing, eight CLI import.meta/CJS, configuration/auth/color/React act and host watcher negative paths; not warning-free.

That full FFT ran **before rebase**, original `6848d57b1535a944c9f9f6ebbe686967f2710520` on dd9713a6e. It is not a full FFT on final 8c. The deliverable explicitly reports post-rebase 57 files/606 tests plus web typecheck and a **17:09 post-rebase web build** for retained pMh2; that build association is author provenance, not a sealed execution-source receipt. Current source and retained BUILD_ID were independently read. Do not infer the retained artifact is stale merely because its preceding full FFT was pre-rebase.

The later exact-a31 descendant FFT provides composed-green evidence for 8c's final base: a31's only changes are the three B6 build/test/comment files, not these runtime implementations. Its complete 4288-line log and exact-head rc=0 receipt were independently audited separately: **556 files / 7331 tests passed / 60 skipped**, all nine configs. Therefore no extra missing-final-composition gate blocker is asserted here. It does not repair the three runtime defects.

Author idle receipts/probes were fully read. In the 60-second comparison, workspace/Pij observed idle actions were **0→0** while their pre-window requests fell 4→0. Browser pre-window requests fell 9→4; its observed idle 4→0 does not control equivalent file-change stimuli. The 120-second baseline's four idle requests were late note requests, not the four Git actions from the 60-second baseline; it has no Pij row. Before base 0aeb and after 8c include intervening changes and different author-reported loads; not isolated performance/FCP proof. No after-dev run exists.

The probe counts only requests with next-action and classifies at>=idleStart without an upper bound; capture continues through screenshot work. It does not record successful responses, exact end timestamps or general network traffic in its result JSON. Zero actions is not zero network/API traffic. Author event probe supports visible burst 1 / simulated-hidden 0 / shown 1 / deletion 1; visibility was property override plus event, not OS backgrounding. It does not cover either short transition defect above or UI freshness. Its visible request arrived 6247 ms after burst start, not a measured two-second end-to-end ceiling.

## Cleanup, diagnostic caveats and next action

Owned 3199 and isolated browser stopped; final lsof found no listener. No terminal sidecar/tmux session was created for this review. A mode-700 private TMPDIR was prepared and its intended private socket resolution observed before Next. No Jordan service or default tmux cleanup occurred. All worktree scaffolds, owned notes, temporary Git repository and NDJSON keys were removed.

Browser diagnostics contain **62 ERR_ABORTED request failures plus one reviewer-injected wait-predicate pageerror**. The latter was `window.__tracePosts.some` after a full-page toolbar refresh discarded the observer; that abandoned attempt is not product proof and was corrected before the successful live file-event observation. No console-error entry was recorded. Do not call this an entirely pageerror-free trace. Full raw diagnostics `/tmp/reviewer-trace-browser-errors.json`.

Author has acknowledged all three P2s and prepared an **uncommitted** correction in `chainglass-trace-idle-fix`, including the second spacing scenario and LOW logging case. No corrective credit until a landed/gated head is reviewed. Release the old 8c reviewer artifact hold. Next: finish queued B6 a31 delivery review, then corrective ctx 69031952b and canonical-nav f23b70f58; review the trace correction once landed.
